title: Silas and the Veil
premise: Rafael Okonkwo has survived three years in the city of Corvane by selling harmless charms and hiding the true depth of her gift, but the crown's new witch-hunt forces her into the tunnels beneath the city with a smuggler's found family who become her first real home. There she learns the truth: King Aldric was bound years ago to an ancient entity called the Veil, which now rules through his body and feeds on the magic it outlawed. To free him, Rafael must unbind a king from the thing wearing his crown—an act that will demand her own power as payment—and she discovers her old mistress, the hedge-witch Serah, helped forge the original binding. In the end Rafael breaks the binding at the cost of her gift, Aldric dies human and free, and Rafael chooses to stay with her found family, learning that power surrendered can be love fulfilled.
about_author: Dominic Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about reluctant magics and chosen families from a cluttered study overlooking a northern harbor.

chapters.title: Charms for the Fearful
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She sells a luck-knot to a dockworker in Corvane's night market while hiding her real talent behind hedge-tricks. When crown criers announce a registry—and then a hunt—for anyone with the gift, her carefully invisible life shatters. Emotional beat: the dread of being seen at last.

chapters.title: The Tunnels Beneath Bellows Street
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Fleeing a sweep of her tenement, she follows a chalk sigil only witches can see down into smuggler tunnels run by Odile Voss, a one-eyed ex-soldier sheltering gifted fugitives. Rafael lies about how strong she is. Emotional beat: wary hope at finding others like herself.

chapters.title: A Family Assembled
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She meets the household: Tam, a boy who hears stone speak; Maretta, a healer burned out of her village; and Jules, Odile's partner, who distrusts newcomers. A shared meal becomes the first family table Rafael has known since running from Serah. Emotional beat: belonging, cautiously accepted.

chapters.title: What the Registry Costs
chapters.summary: Jules's POV. A registered neighbor is taken, and his shop burns with him inside it. Jules argues they must flee Corvane; Odile refuses to abandon those still hiding. Rafael quietly heals Tam's broken hand, revealing more power than she intended. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The King Who Does Not Sleep
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV, the first glimpse inside the palace. The king watches his own hands sign death warrants, aware something else moves them—the Veil, coiled beneath his will since a bargain struck in his youth. He leaves coded messages in state documents, praying someone reads them. Emotional beat: horror of captivity within one's own body.

chapters.title: The Message in the Margins
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The boy who hears stone finds one of Aldric's smuggled pleas embedded in a confiscated ledger Odile's crew stole. The tunnel family debates whether it's a trap. Rafael recognizes the binding-script—it matches work she saw in Serah's grimoire. Emotional beat: the past reaching for her.

chapters.title: Serah's Grimoire
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Flashback interwoven with present: three years ago, Rafael fled after discovering Serah's oldest book contained diagrams for binding a living king. Now she admits to Odile what she knows, and the family decides someone must reach the palace archive for the counter-ritual. Emotional beat: guilt confessed, burden shared.

chapters.title: The Hunt Closes
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Veil's hunters—witch-sniffers called the Grey Cloaks—raid the tunnels' upper entrances. The family scatters along escape routes; Maretta is captured buying time for the others. Odile blames herself. Emotional beat: the cost of sheltering others made flesh.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Thieves
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. To reach the palace, Rafael bargains with Corvane's crime-lord, Mother Quill, trading a charm of true luck—a dangerous working that drains her badly. Jules, who lost family to Quill's rivals, helps anyway, and their enmity thaws. Emotional beat: trust built through shared risk.

chapters.title: Into the Palace Dark
chapters.summary: Rafael and Jules infiltrate the palace during a masked feast. Rafael senses the Veil's hunger saturating the stones; servants move like sleepwalkers. In the royal library she finds the counter-ritual—and learns the unbinding requires a witch of sufficient power to take the binding into herself. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The Veil senses an intruder witch and rides Aldric's body to hunt her through the corridors. Rafael faces the king—possessed, terrible—and glimpses the man trapped behind his own eyes pleading silently. She escapes by burning her stored charms. Emotional beat: terror mixed with pity.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Returning to the main tunnel home, they find it razed; Tam is missing, taken by the Grey Cloaks as bait. Odile must choose between rescuing the boy and supporting Rafael's mission, and chooses both, splitting the family. Emotional beat: fury and maternal grief.

chapters.title: Prison of Salt and Iron
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. In a Grey Cloak cell, Tam endures interrogation, protected by the stones whispering him calm. He learns the Cloaks answer not to the crown but directly to the Veil—and that Maretta lives, held nearby. Emotional beat: small courage against vast cruelty.

chapters.title: Two Rescues
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael and Jules raid the prison; Odile creates a diversion that nearly kills her. They pull out Tam and Maretta, but Rafael overdraws her power healing Odile's wounds, leaving herself hollowed and vulnerable. Emotional beat: love proven in blood and exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Old Mistress
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Following the grimoire's clues, the family seeks Serah in the marshlands—and Rafael confronts the woman who raised her. Serah confesses she helped bind Aldric decades ago, believing she was caging a greater evil, and that the Veil has corrupted the binding since. Emotional beat: betrayal, forgiveness half-granted.

chapters.title: How to Unmake a King's Chains
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah teaches the unbinding: it must be done at the binding-stone beneath the throne, and the witch who works it takes the Veil's chains into her own soul unless another vessel freely accepts them. Rafael volunteers; Serah insists it should be her penance. Emotional beat: two generations arguing over who deserves to be sacrificed.

chapters.title: The March on Corvane
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Veil, sensing the threat, declares martial law and begins public burnings to bait remaining witches. The found family walks back toward a city on fire, gathering freed fugitives into a ragged column. Emotional beat: dread transformed into purpose.

chapters.title: Storming the Binding-Stone
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Through sewers and betrayed passwords, the family fights to the chamber beneath the throne where the original binding-stone pulses. Serah holds the Grey Cloaks off at terrible cost; Jules carries the wounded; Rafael reaches the stone alone. Emotional beat: everything staked on one desperate door.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Alternating Rafael and Aldric POVs. Rafael begins the unbinding as the Veil abandons Aldric's failing body to crush her directly. Inside the binding, she speaks to the trapped king, and he gives her the last strength of his mortal will. Emotional beat: intimacy forged between two strangers in the dark.

chapters.title: The Price of the Crown
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The unbinding completes: the Veil is chained into Rafael's offered vessel—but Aldric, emptied of the thing that kept him alive these twenty years, dies in her arms, free and grateful. Rafael survives, but her gift is gone, burned away as payment. Emotional beat: victory inseparable from mourning.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. With the Veil caged and the Grey Cloaks leaderless, Corvane staggers toward lifting the magic ban. Odile tends the wounded family, buries Serah, and realizes Rafael—powerless, unregistered, ordinary—is staying by choice, not necessity. Emotional beat: quiet recognition that family needs no magic to hold.

chapters.title: Silas and the Veil
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Months later, Rafael runs a stall selling honest, charmless goods above rebuilt tunnels, teaching frightened young witches that their gift is not their worth. Deep beneath the city, the binding-stone hums with what she carries, watched over by everyone she loves. Emotional beat: peace earned, power redefined as the people you choose.
